statusText: CME equity futures are halted for seventeen of the twenty-four published hours, which holds Tail at the floor of a closed venue. No U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside this window, leaving the 22:00Z Sunday restart as the only slot carrying materially elevated conditional risk, and this weekend's news set is two-sided rather than aligned.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail of 5 sits far below the 25% block threshold and no danger window is identified, because the current hour falls inside the weekend futures halt and no live NQ price path exists to assess. headline: CME equity futures stay halted through seventeen of the twenty-four published hours while the weekend delivers a genuinely two-sided set: a first Houthi ballistic missile intercepted over Riyadh and an uncorroborated claim against Aramco's Yanbu facilities, against CENTCOM reporting Hormuz throughput at a six-month high and Iran conveying terms for talks via Qatar
body:
Seventeen of the 24 hours published here fall inside the CME weekend halt; the final seven contain the 22:00Z restart and the Asian hours that follow it. Cash equities closed Friday 18 September at 20:00Z and there has been no live NQ price path since. Friday's marks were re-verified at primary sources for this run: the Nasdaq-100 settled 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% against a previous close of 29,447.00, finishing 3.63 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. The session was rotational rather than uniform - Broadcom rose about 3% and Micron about 3.9% while Meta fell about 2.4% and Oracle about 2% - and the Dow closed 95 points lower even as the Nasdaq gained 0.7%. Friday was also a quarterly triple-witching expiry. That divided internal picture is why no structural Tail amplifier is carried into this window: the last observed session was split, not one-way.

The macro backdrop is unchanged and hawkish. The FOMC raised the target range 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September in a unanimous 12-0 vote. The H.15 release dated 18 September shows the 2-year at 4.67%, the 10-year at 4.94% and the 30-year at 5.29% as of 17 September, with the effective federal funds rate at 3.88%. Against that, VIX closed at 14.81, down 4.08% and near the lower end of its 13.38-35.30 annual range, so the options market ended the week without stress pricing. Crude settled easier for a third consecutive session, WTI at 100.30 and Brent at 103.87, though WTI remains up about 18.85% over the month because Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline has been offline since the 11 September strike and Aramco suspended loadings at the Red Sea port of Yanbu on 15 September.

What separates this run from the previous ones is that weekend reporting is now balanced on both sides rather than leaning de-escalatory. U.S. Central Command said on Saturday that oil and gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz over the past fortnight reached a six-month high, that the primary transit lanes are clear of mines, that more than one billion barrels have moved out of the Persian Gulf in roughly two months and that over 2,000 commercial transits have been escorted. Against that, Saudi Arabia issued its first air-raid alerts for Riyadh since the renewal of fighting: a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at the capital was reported intercepted, a fuel depot fire near King Khalid International Airport was extinguished, and the airport saw significant flight disruption. The Houthis separately claimed strikes on Aramco facilities at Yanbu, a claim Saudi authorities described as thwarted and which no confirmed damage report has yet corroborated; because Yanbu loadings were already suspended on 15 September, an uncorroborated claim adds little incremental supply loss to what Friday's tape had already absorbed. Reporting timelines for the pipeline itself remain in conflict, framed in days by U.S. officials and in weeks by Saudi officials. On the diplomatic side, Iran conveyed conditions for re-engagement through Qatari intermediaries covering an end to the war, the release of frozen assets and the lifting of the naval blockade, while Turkiye stated its backing for Saudi security and a Saudi-led naval coalition prepared to secure Red Sea waterways.

A weekend that is escalatory and de-escalatory at once is the classic setup for two-way price discovery at the reopen rather than a persistent one-way path, and under the risk definition used here conflicting evidence lifts Stress ahead of Tail. Stress is therefore published at 29, up from the previous run, while current Tail stays at the closed-venue floor of 5 because no venue is open and no structure has been observed. Confidence is published at 74: the evidence set is broad and freshly verified across index levels, volatility, yields, crude and the calendar, and the one genuinely missing input is a live price path, which no weekend assessment can hold.

No U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside the published 24 hours. The first Monday catalyst, Goolsbee's remarks at 10:30Z, sits beyond the end of the window, and the first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Tokyo cash equities open at 00:00Z and provide the first regional cash reference since Friday, with the Bank of Japan's policy rate at 1.25%, its highest since 1995, the standing conditional for Asian risk appetite. Tail is published at 5 through the early halt, drifting up in single steps that track time-to-restart rather than observed structure, and reaching a window high of 16 across the restart and its first full hour before easing through the Asian session. Every published hour stays inside the low Tail band and the EA_ON mapping, and no danger window is identified.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail held 5 through the first seventeen slots and 4 across the final seven. Stress opened at 21, held a 21 plateau through the morning, drifted through 22, 23 and 24 across the afternoon and evening, peaked at 26 shortly after midnight and eased to 25 in the closing hours. Dominant mode was normal in all 24 hours because no venue was open to produce classifiable structure. Confidence started at 81, decayed steadily to a 72 trough late in the Saturday session as distance from the Friday tape grew, then recovered to 76 in the final hour as weekend reporting was corroborated.
outlookSummary: Seventeen of the 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt; the final seven contain the 22:00Z restart and the Asian hours after it. Cash closed 20:00Z Friday and CME equity futures reopen at 22:00Z Sunday, 18:00 ET. No U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside this window; the next U.S. catalyst is the Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z Monday, beyond its end, and the first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Tail holds 5 through the early halt, steps to 6 from 07:00Z, 7 from 10:00Z, 8 from 13:00Z, 9 from 15:00Z, 10 from 17:00Z, 11 at 19:00Z, 12 at 20:00Z and 13 at 21:00Z, then reaches a window high of 16 across the 22:00Z restart and its first full hour before easing to 15, 14, 13, 12 and 11 through the Asian session. That drift tracks time-to-restart rather than observed structure and stays inside the low band and the EA_ON mapping for every published hour. Mode is published as event/whipsaw for the restart and the hour after it, then mixed for the first three Asian hours, reflecting expected two-way discovery against a weekend that produced escalation and diplomacy at the same time; it returns to normal for the final two hours on the base case that repricing has cleared.
